Peptides in North Las Vegas, NV

D2C Peptides ships research peptides and lab supplies to North Las Vegas, Nevada's third most populous city, from the USA and Canada.1 The city's own NOAA station averages 85.4 days a year at or above 100 °F, more than the airport's 78.2,23 so this page covers keeping vials cool, dark and sealed.

Shipping to North Las Vegas

Orders to North Las Vegas ship from the USA and Canada and follow the shipping policy used for every order across the United States. Seven ZIP code areas lie almost entirely inside the city: 89030, 89031, 89032, 89081, 89084, 89085 and 89086. ZIP 89115 is split, with 43 percent of its land in the city, and about 35 percent of the city's land lies in no ZIP code area at all, per the Census Bureau's 2020 relationship file.12 Delivery problems go to the returns page, certificates of analysis appear on the lab results page as each one becomes available, and the contact page takes questions.

Keeping peptides cool in North Las Vegas

North Las Vegas has its own NOAA normals station, N LAS VEGAS, whose coordinates the Census Geocoder places inside city limits;5 NOAA lists it at 578.5 meters, about 1,898 feet, above sea level.6 It averages 85.4 days a year at or above 100 °F, more than the LAS VEGAS WFO station (82.8) or the airport (78.2), though NOAA built those counts from 17, 20 and 29 years of records respectively.243 July averages a high of 105.7 °F and a low of 79.3 °F.6 June to August highs average 103.5 °F, and the station counts 142.4 days a year at or above 90 °F.2 Winter is mild: January averages 60.9 °F by day and 38.0 °F at night, and precipitation totals 4.27 inches a year.62

Heat is not the only exposure to manage. GenScript, a peptide maker, says sequences containing Cys, Met or Trp are prone to oxidation and need storage with little or no oxygen, so it advises limiting air exposure and keeping vials tightly capped.8 Bachem, another maker, says those same amino acids need special care against oxidation when a peptide is dissolved, calling for oxygen-free water or buffers, or reducing agents.1314 Add the light advice from makers and labels, and the routine is simple: bring the parcel in from the heat, keep vials boxed and sealed, and open them only when needed. The storage guide and the reconstitution guide cover the details.

About North Las Vegas

North Las Vegas is an incorporated city with 105.35 square miles of land.15 The Census Bureau estimated 296,653 residents on July 1, 2025, up about 14 percent from an April 2020 base of 259,479, which works out to about 2,816 people per square mile.115 Nevada's certified estimate is 292,114 and the county's August 2025 estimate is 294,125.1617 About three in four residents live in single-family homes, 220,641 of them in the county's count, and another 35,408 live in apartments.17

The city skews young. Its median age is 34.2 years, with 25.5 percent of residents under 18 and 12.1 percent 65 or older, against a county median of 38.5 (ACS 2020 to 2024).1819 Residents are 41.7 percent Hispanic or Latino, 23.4 percent non-Hispanic White, 20.6 percent non-Hispanic Black and 7.0 percent non-Hispanic Asian.18 About 3,099 residents serve in the Armed Forces, and 8.6 percent of civilian adults are veterans.2021 By industry, 19.2 percent of employed residents work in arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation and food services, 16.8 percent in education, health care and social assistance, and 9.7 percent in construction.20

Several health and education institutions use the city's name or address. CMS lists three hospitals with North Las Vegas addresses: North Vista Hospital, a private non-profit acute care hospital with emergency services; the St. Rose Dominican North Las Vegas campus, an acute care hospital with emergency services under proprietary ownership; and the VA Southern Nevada Healthcare System.22 The VA's North Las Vegas VA Medical Center opened on April 15, 2013 as a 90-bed inpatient facility of over one million square feet, built on 150 acres the Bureau of Land Management transferred to the VA in 2004.23 The College of Southern Nevada runs a North Las Vegas Campus and also lists a Nellis AFB Center.24 The VA's ties to military medicine go back further: in 1994 it became a full partner with the Air Force's 99th Medical Group and managed 57 of the 114 beds at the newly built Mike O'Callaghan Federal Hospital.23

Frequently asked questions

Is North Las Vegas part of Las Vegas?

No. North Las Vegas is a separate incorporated city, and with 296,653 residents in the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate it ranks third in Nevada, behind Las Vegas and Henderson and ahead of Reno.1 It has its own page here for that reason, while the Las Vegas hub covers the valley as a whole. Orders to either city ship from the USA and Canada on the same terms.

Is North Las Vegas hotter than other parts of the valley?

By NOAA's counts of 100 °F days, yes. The N LAS VEGAS station, inside the city, averages 85.4 days a year at or above 100 °F, against 82.8 at the LAS VEGAS WFO station and 78.2 at the airport (1991 to 2020 normals, built from 17, 20 and 29 years of records).2435 Its July nights run cooler, though: 79.3 °F against 82.0 °F at the airport.67

Should vials delivered to North Las Vegas be kept out of the light?

Yes. Peptide makers and product labels both point that way. GenScript advises storing freeze-dried peptides at -20 °C away from bright light.8 The FDA labels for several approved freeze-dried products, EGRIFTA SV, EGRIFTA WR and ZOMACTON, tell users to keep the vials in the original carton to protect them from light.91011 Keeping research vials boxed and out of sunlight follows the same logic.
